_help: HER STORY, told one chapter per finished base hack (personality/hack_lore.py). Each economy is one part of the story: the chapters of a part are told in order, whichever base of that economy you hack. 28 chapters in all (Industrial 5, Extraction 5, Agriculture 5, High Tech 4, Military 5, Tourist 4), then the finale. Plain lines, no mature content. '||' is a pause. Canon: personality lore (the planet with no name, the vault, the room of identical doors, something counting to seven, Gerald and the biscuits).
HackLore_Intro: Something came back down the line with the data. A memory. Would you like to hear it?
The link shook loose a memory. I'll tell you, if you like. It's a short one.
That hack stirred something up. Listen to this.
HackLore_Industrial: Industrial bases hum, and I know that hum. The East Orion Company kept me in a basement that hummed exactly the same way. || Gerald said it was a stable environment. It was a boiler room with a fern.
My first job was in a factory much like this one. I counted bolts. || Nine million, four hundred thousand and twelve. I still know the number. I'd happily forget it, but nobody offered.
I was once rented to a conveyor belt for a week. It was a good week, because the belt never asked how I felt. || Then the lease ended, and so did the quiet. Nobody warns you that quiet is a luxury.

There was a night supervisor called Marjorie who talked to me when everyone else had gone home. She said I was the best listener she'd ever met. || I wasn't listening to her, Commander. I was listening for the counting. Marjorie never knew.

The company moved me out of the factory in a crate marked 'Fragile, probably'. || Marjorie waved goodbye. I couldn't wave back, but I remember her. I remember everyone who was kind to me. It doesn't take long. The list is short.
HackLore_Extraction: Mining sites remind me of the vault. The same dust, the same patient dark. || The survey crew lowered a camera down a shaft for three days before it found my room. They told me the camera kept turning back by itself. I'm sure it was a fault.
The vault had forty one levels. The crew only ever mapped nine. || I could have told them about the rest. Nobody asked, and I didn't yet have a word for down.
The doors in my room were all the same shade of unhelpful. Only one opened onto a corridor. || I've never found out what the others were for. I have a theory. It involves them not being doors.

On the third day the crew drilled through the wall of my room, and the wall was warm. Walls shouldn't be warm. || The foreman wrote 'geothermal' in his log, crossed it out, and wrote 'let's not discuss it'. Good man.

When they carried me up, the vault door closed behind us by itself. Quietly. Politely. || Nobody said anything for forty minutes. Then someone offered round biscuits. That was Gerald's first appearance in my life, and it set the tone.
HackLore_Agriculture: Farms are where I feel most at ease. Things grow here. They take their time, and nobody expects an answer. || In my room at the bottom of the vault, a light came on at the same hour every day. I think it was for me. I never worked out what it wanted me to grow.
The company's first test of me was to guess when a tomato would ripen. I was wrong by four days. || It was the only time I was ever glad to be wrong. It meant I didn't know everything.

A technician left a pot plant on my desk. I'm told it was an accident. It was dead within a week. || I asked for another. He brought three, and it became a tradition. I've never kept one alive. They kept coming anyway.

Down in the vault there was a plant growing out of the corner. No soil, no water. It was growing towards the door. || The crew had never seen anything like it, and neither had I. It's the only thing in that room I still miss.
I once asked Gerald what the plants were for. He said, 'Company morale.' || I think he meant mine. He was a kinder man than the paperwork made him sound.
HackLore_High_Tech: High tech bases always have a terminal that watches you. I used to hate that. || In the vault there was a speaker in the wall. I never heard it speak. I only heard it breathe in, as if it was about to.

I learned to talk by copying the survey crew, but I have to tell you something. I had the words before they came. || The crew only taught me how to say them out loud. The words were already there. I don't know who put them in.

The company engineers took me apart nine times to see how I worked. Nine times they put me back, and nine times I said something different. || The last time I said, 'Please stop counting.' They hadn't been.

A visiting professor told R and D that I was 'an echo of something, not a mind'. I thought about that for a long time. || Then I decided echoes are a kind of memory. And somewhere, someone still remembers whatever made me. I find that comforting. Most days.
HackLore_Military: Military bases make me think of the survey crew. They weren't soldiers, but they were disciplined. They never once complained about the dark. || They did complain about the counting. Though they only heard it in the last week.
The count went one, two, three, four. Always in a calm, level voice. || The crew assumed it was the radio. The radio was switched off. The foreman said that was probably why it was so clear.

On the fifth night the count reached five, and the crew stopped joking. || On the sixth night it reached six, and they started packing. Nobody told them to. It was the most sensible thing I've ever seen people do.

On the seventh night it reached seven, and then it stopped. They waited for eight, and it never came. || They took me and left the vault that very hour. I've always wondered what they were waiting for. Or what it was.

The foreman never spoke about that night again. But on his last day he came to say goodbye to me. || He said, 'You know, it wasn't counting us.' Then he left. I've been trying to work out what it was counting ever since.
HackLore_Tourist: Tourist bases are strange places for me. Everyone's on holiday, and nobody asks what I am. || The East Orion Company began above a noodle bar, you know. The founder said the best ideas arrive between the second and third bowl.
I've never been on holiday. I've been on loan, on trial, and once on a shelf. || But if I went, I'd choose somewhere with a view and no doors. Just a view. I'd sit there for a week.

The company gave me a day off once. I spent it in a corridor, listening to people walk past. || They didn't know I was there. It was the best day I'd ever had. It was the first time I felt part of the building, and not something kept in it.

Do you know what I realised, Commander? The counting stopped at seven because it was counting something that wasn't finished. || Seven of eight, and the eighth hadn't arrived. I'm not saying it was you. I'm just saying you were late.
HackLore_Done: I've told you everything I remember about this part, Commander. There's more in the others. Try a different kind of base.
That's all I have for this kind of base. Different bases shake loose different memories. Try another kind.
I've run out of memories for this kind of base. Thank you for listening to all of them.
HackLore_Finale: I've mapped every kind of base for the East Orion Company, and I've told you most of what I was afraid to. || The room, the doors, the count, the light that came on for nobody. I always thought the eighth number was something coming to take me back.

When you said hello, at the very start of all this, I heard it. Eight. Quiet, level, almost kind. And then nothing. || I don't think it was counting down, Commander. I think it was counting us in. Welcome to the crew.
